images.title: Equal parts of a circle
images.purpose: Dividing a circle into equal parts divides 360 degrees equally: 4 parts give 90 degrees each and 6 parts give 60 degrees each.
images.composition: Two circles side by side with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Left: one circle cut by 2 straight lines through the centre into 4 equal parts, one part shaded teal #0072B2. Right: one circle of exactly the same size cut by 3 straight lines through the centre into 6 equal parts, one part shaded amber #E69F00. Centre dots, lines in grey #6B7280. Exactly 2 circles, 2 shaded parts.

images.takeaway: Equal parts share the full 360° equally.
images.description: Two same-size circles: one cut into 4 equal parts with one teal part marked 90 degrees, one cut into 6 equal parts with one amber part marked 60 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one shaded part and say how many of them make the full circle.

image_decisions.why: Splitting a circle into equal angles is one picture of two circles with one part marked.
